candidate.Reason: Direct conversion of Bytes to int using toInt() method without proper bounds checking for negative values. When shiftAmount represents a value between 2^31 and 2^32-1 (approximately 2-4 billion), toInt() will convert it to a negative integer due to signed integer overflow, causing incorrect shift behavior.

The toInt() method performs signed conversion from Bytes to int, which can cause negative values when the shift amount represents a value larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE (2^31-1). For shift amounts between approximately 2 billion and 4 billion, this will result in negative values that affect the shift operation logic.

The toInt() method converts Bytes to a signed 32-bit integer, which can cause negative values when the shift amount exceeds 2^31 (approximately 2 billion bits), leading to incorrect shift operations. This is a signed type coercion error where large unsigned values become negative signed integers.
